pr_title: Fix re-connect logic in Apple TV integration
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
If the connection to an Apple TV breaks for some reason, e.g. network not available anymore, it will be "disconnected" within Home Assistant which will stop the re-connect loop. An unstable network connection might thus break the Apple TV integration and a lot of people are experiencing this. This minor change fixes that by keeping the re-connect loop running in the background until the connection is re-established.

I believe this fixes ##135964, but I have not managed to reproduce that bug exactly.

issue_context.title: I  have to reload my Apple TV integration every so often because it becomes unresponsive
issue_context.body:
The Apple TV integration becomes unresponsive - a re-load temporarily fixes it. 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2025.1.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Apple TV 

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

It works great until it doesn't.  Any command to Apple TV 4k stops working.  As soon as I go to the Apple TV integration and re-load, everything if fine - sometimes for a week, sometimes less.


I found that after restart and clicking a bit, the state and attributes in dev tools are just frozen and never updated on any action until the next HA restart.

As a temporary solution, I fond that remote restart + 1 second waiting helps:

```
  - target:
      entity_id: remote.salon
    action: remote.turn_off
    data: {}
  - target:
      entity_id: remote.salon
    action: remote.turn_on
    data: {}
  - delay:
      hours: 0
      minutes: 0
      seconds: 1
      milliseconds: 0
```

I'm finally gonna try to fix this, but I have some problem reproducing the behavior exactly. If I set everything up and disable network on my computer, I can see the device time out and disconnecting. The re-connect loop is disabled because the device is set to "disconnected", I.e. it is set to off (when checking the remote or media player entity). Can anyone confirm if this is the case? Also, if it is off, what happens of you turn it on? Any logs?
I belive #139289 might fix this. If anyone can test it that would be great.

@postlund from my personal experience & questions I've asked from people experiencing this on reddit it only seems to happen with ATVs connected over ethernet. When the device goes in standby it seems to do some weird stuff to the network connection, including getting blocked by enterprise network gear (experience this myself, see: https://community.ui.com/questions/Blocked-by-STP-to-prevent-network-loop-issue-with-second-Apple-TV-in-Unifi-network/0cd57dc0-0611-4133-8abe-0739b50d52e1)

The only real solution so far I've seen posted, but have not yet had time to confirm, is to make sure the ATV is joined to Homekit
My ATV is joined to HomeKit and I still have the issue. I do use Ethernet.

I've updated to 2025.3.1 and the issue seems to persist. 

As others have mentioned, as a workaround you can cycle the remote off and on again:

```
actions:
  - type: turn_off
    entity_id: <goes here>
    domain: remote
  - delay:
      hours: 0
      minutes: 0
      seconds: 0
      milliseconds: 50
  - type: turn_on
    entity_id: <goes here>
    domain: remote
```
